data.narrative:
Xtend, a Series B defense and security company founded by Aviv Shapira, has raised $100M to date. The valuation analysis employs a comparables universe of 10 companies—2 public (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) and 8 private peers—all operating in the Defense & Security sector at similar stages.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using total raised as a proxy base of $100M and applying a typical Series B step-up multiplier of 1.9x, yields $190M. Peer-median valuation across six same-stage, same-sector comparables—Dream Security ($3.0B), Harmattan AI ($1.4B), Code Metal ($1.2B), Defense Unicorns ($1.0B), Heven AeroTech ($1.0B), and one additional peer—produced a median of $1.1B, with a range spanning $300M to $3.0B.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $162M (low) to $1.3B (high), with a median of $658M. The wide dispersion reflects material uncertainty in comparable company selection: the peer set exhibits significant heterogeneity, with the top performer valued at 10x the minimum. Stage-progression conservatively anchors below the peer median, suggesting either that Xtend lags peer maturity metrics (revenue, customer concentration, or defensibility) or that peer valuations embed sector-specific premiums not yet reflected in Xtend's fundamentals. Resolution of revenue traction and customer diversification would materially narrow this range.
